items.title: Nifty's recovery or just another trap? Analysts split on market's future direction!
items.description: Nifty's recent recovery has generated optimism, but a sustained close above key resistance is crucial for further gains. Analysts suggest a cautious approach with potential accumulation of certain stocks during dips. Key stocks for investment include Aurobindo Pharma and TCS, which display strong price momentum and resilience. Market participants are advised to monitor immediate support levels for Nifty and Bank Nifty.

items.title: Stock Radar: TD Power Systems retreats after hitting fresh record high in October 2026. Time to buy or book profits?
items.description: TD Power Systems shares have gained nearly 40% in three months, trading above key moving averages. Technical experts see further upside towards Rs 935 in the next few weeks, with momentum indicators supporting the bullish outlook.

items.title: DBS Chief sees overseas confidence in India despite capital outflow concerns
items.description: DBS Bank CEO Tan Su Shan emphasized the strong demand for FCNR(B) deposits as investor confidence in India. She highlighted India's potential for foreign direct investment and its advantageous position in the artificial intelligence sector. Despite foreign net sales affecting the rupee, she remains optimistic about India's economic growth and digital infrastructure. Tan discussed the importance of promoting FDI and exports to stabilize currency levels.

items.title: Swan Defence shares rise 4% to hit 52-week high on Rs 1,897 crore tanker order prospect
items.description: Swan Defence and Heavy Industries shares rose after the company emerged as the lowest bidder for a Rs 1,897 crore order to build four medium-range product tankers. The proposed contract could strengthen its order book amid India's push to revive domestic shipbuilding.

items.title: Why is market falling today? Sensex slumps over 500 points, Nifty below 22,400. 5 key factors behind selloff
items.description: The Indian stock market saw a downturn as both Sensex and Nifty lost previously gained ground. Market confidence was shaken by ongoing FII selling and increasing bond yields. Tech Mahindra experienced the most significant drop, with shares down nearly 4%. Conversely, the broader market segments like Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 performed well, showcasing resilience amidst the decline in major companies.

items.title: Tech Picks: Trent, Physicswallah among 5 stocks to buy for up to 23% returns
items.description: The Indian stock market traded on a mixed note on Monday, with the Sensex slipping into the red while the Nifty held on to gains. A mix of headwinds and tailwinds kept investors cautious, following last week’s positive close that ended an eight-week losing streak. Given the prevailing market conditions, analysts treat the current rebound as a relief rally until the index demonstrates sustained strength above key resistance levels. Here are 5 stock recommendations for decent returns in the short term:

items.title: Lenskart Solutions shares crack 5% after Rs 1,985-crore block deal; Alpha Wave likely sells take
items.description: Lenskart Solutions reported a 182.3% YoY jump in Q1 FY27 net profit to Rs 228 crore, while revenue rose 33.6% to Rs 2,214 crore. EBITDA margin expanded to 21.7% as product margins crossed 70% for the first time. Growth remained broad-based across India and international markets, with offerings ranging from Rs 500 glasses to premium eyewear.

items.title: PC Jeweller shares jump 5% to fresh 52-week high, market value swells by Rs 2,500 crore in 4 sessions
items.description: PC Jeweller shares hit a fresh 52-week high, extending a four-session rally to 20%. The stock has gained 64% in 2026 so far, supported by renewed investor optimism after the company repaid its outstanding debt ahead of schedule and achieved debt-free status.

items.title: 63 Moons Technologies shares rally 9% as subsidiary raises FY27 revenue guidance to Rs 600 crore
items.description: Shares of 63 Moons Technologies rallied after subsidiary 63SATS Cybertech reported Rs 218 crore in first-half FY27 billings and raised its full-year billed revenue guidance to Rs 600 crore from Rs 350 crore, citing strong execution and a growing business pipeline.

items.title: Crude oil, rupee & interest rates: Is the macroeconomic squeeze spreading to equities?
items.description: Indian equities are currently facing significant challenges, including the impact of elevated crude oil prices and currency depreciation. Analysts highlight that these factors are leading to inflationary pressures and potential monetary tightening. While foreign investor outflows are also affecting market sentiment, some analysts believe that corporate earnings may stabilize the market. Preferred sectors include financials, power, and consumer discretionary, expected to remain resilient amid broader market weakness.

items.title: Suzlon Energy shares drop 30% in a year, but Motilal Oswal screams Buy. Here's why it sees 73% upside
items.description: Suzlon Energy shares have declined nearly 30% in a year, but Motilal Oswal retains a Buy rating with a target price of Rs 65, implying 73% upside. The brokerage expects stronger second-half FY27 earnings, supported by rising deliveries and a robust order book.

items.title: Sensex falls 500 points, Nifty below 22,400. What can trigger a sharp rally on Dalal Street?
items.description: The Indian stock market has encountered a setback following a brief recovery, influenced by external dynamics and investor sentiment. Both the Sensex and Nifty experienced declines, yet certain broader market indicators revealed upward trends. Analysts highlighted that elevating crude oil rates and US bond yields were pivotal in shaping market fluctuations. Investors are urged to focus on Nifty's technical support levels and seek potential long-term gains.

items.title: Meesho shares surge 5% as strong festive sales, Q2 biz update boost sentiment. Should you buy?
items.description: Meesho shares rallied as much as 5% after the company reported a 75% year-on-year jump in Day 1 orders during its Mega Blockbuster Sale 2026. Orders on Meesho Mall surged over 200%, while creator-led commerce grew 3.7 times. Meanwhile, Nomura initiated coverage with a Reduce rating, citing rising competition, while UBS raised its target price by 24% to Rs 260.

items.title: Will RBI’s CRR hike to 99% hit HDFC, SBI and other bank stocks? Here’s what Jefferies says
items.description: The RBI has raised the minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement to 99% from 90% from October 16 to curb banking system liquidity. Jefferies expects a limited impact on banks’ net interest margins, estimating a potential 1-2 basis point increase in funding costs. It prefers banks over NBFCs in a rising-rate environment and sees up to 47% upside in Bandhan Bank.

items.title: Iran war’s end will be turning point for India, Amundi arm says
items.description: Amundi Investment Institute sees potential for Indian equities to rebound if the Iran war ends, easing oil pressures. Despite foreign outflows and a nearly 14% Nifty decline, improving investment, resilient demand and 7.1% growth projections support optimism, particularly for defence and manufacturing stocks.

items.title: HCL Tech shares rise 2% ahead of IT major’s Q2 earnings announcement today. What to expect?
items.description: HCL Technologies shares rose ahead of the IT major’s Q2 FY27 results, with brokerages expecting around 12% year-on-year growth in net profit and 16% growth in revenue. Acquisitions, deal ramp-ups and seasonal strength are likely to support performance, while investors will watch for a revision in the company’s guidance.

items.title: Echoes of 2017: Why domestic flows alone won't rescue Indian equities
items.description: Strong domestic inflows through SIPs and mutual funds are failing to sustain Indian equity returns amid continuous FII selling and moderating earnings growth. Drawing parallels to the 2017 market cycle, this analysis highlights why structural macroeconomic challenges and valuation compression demand a strategic shift toward high-quality, largecap stocks.

items.title: Top Nifty50 stocks analysts suggest buying in this volatile week
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, is a comprehensive report that evaluates five key components of 4,000+ listed stocks – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: From paneer to pizza, FSSAI puts India’s ₹200 lakh crore consumer boom to the test. Who pays?
items.description: The FSSAI's escalated enforcement in consumer sectors in India has led to increased compliance costs for companies. Many brands are now reevaluating their product claims and formulations as they face regulatory pressure. This heightened scrutiny could lead to rising operational costs and may require pricing changes for consumers. The increased compliance standards will likely benefit organized companies while posing significant challenges for smaller, unregulated businesses over time.

items.title: Market Trading Guide: Astra Microwave, Manappuram among 5 stock recommendations for Tuesday
items.description: Indian markets failed to hold early gains on Monday as sentiment weakened amid a rise in the 10-year bond yield to a three-year high and continued FII outflows driven by external uncertainties. Going forward, analysts say the Middle East remains a key overhang, with continued Houthi attacks on Saudi and regional energy infrastructure keeping concerns over potential supply disruptions and elevated crude oil prices alive.Here are 5 stock recommendations for Tuesday

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Tuesday
items.description: Indian benchmark indices reversed early gains on Monday, with the Sensex falling 548 points and the Nifty closing below 22,400 amid persistent FII selling, rising bond yields and geopolitical concerns. Investors will track key stocks, global cues, crude oil prices, inflation data and earnings expectations for Tuesday’s market direction.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: An IT major for a 5.7% upmove, a mid-cap iron and steel maker’s stock for a rise of almost 6%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: PVR Inox among 4 stocks hitting 52-week highs; rallied up to 13% in a month
items.description: Benchmark Sensex slipped 548 points to close at 71,924. Despite the broader market decline, four stocks from the BSE 500 index touched fresh 52-week highs, reaching their highest price levels in the past year. A 52-week high represents the highest price at which a stock has traded over the previous 12 months and may indicate increased trading activity and investor interest.

items.title: Market wrap: ITC, Apollo Hospital, Dr Reddy's Labs, Bajaj Auto top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Monday
items.description: Indian equity markets ended lower on Monday as rising bond yields and continued FII outflows weighed on sentiment. The Nifty fell 0.70% to 22,363, while the Sensex lost 0.76% to 71,925. FMCG stocks led sectoral losses, while auto stocks gained. Dr Reddy’s and Bajaj Auto topped Nifty gainers.

items.title: Elara initiates coverage on Adani Power, sees  up to 17% upside as expansion plans gather pace
items.description: Elara Securities has initiated coverage on Adani Power with an Accumulate rating and a target price of Rs 220, implying 17% upside. The brokerage expects capacity expansion from 18.3 GW to around 42 GW by FY32 to drive growth, while flagging execution risks, rising debt and limited valuation headroom.

items.title: Jefferies sees 35% upside in Adani Green shares, flags demand and execution triggers
items.description: Jefferies has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Adani Green Energy, setting a target price of Rs 1,695, implying 35% upside from the recent close of Rs 1,255. The brokerage sees the stock’s 22% correction from its peak as an opportunity, citing attractive valuations, rising power demand, improving utilisation at Khavda and expansion in battery storage.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.

items.title: Sunil Singhania adds new stock to portfolio in Q2 after 140% rally; likely exits Cyient DLM
items.description: Veteran investor Sunil Singhania's Abakkus Flexi Cap Fund acquired a 1.15% stake in Aether Industries and raised its holdings in Heritage Foods during Q2 FY27. Meanwhile, the fund appears to have exited Cyient DLM as its holding dropped below 1% following a sharp multi-month rally.

items.title: Smallcaps have surged 2.3x since April 2023. Why Vikas Khemani still sees India’s next multibaggers here
items.description: Smallcaps have surged 2.3 times since April 2023, but Carnelian Capital founder Vikas Khemani believes the segment still offers India’s next multibaggers. Despite elevated valuations, stronger earnings growth, greater domestic exposure, and a wider pool of high-growth businesses could create opportunities for investors who focus on stock selection and management quality.

items.title: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 34% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: Given the current global and domestic situation, the chances are that the volatility quotient in the market will remain high. So, the best option is to sit on the sidelines and let the situation settle. The problem with waiting, however, is that the situation may not settle for quite some time. Why? Because the players involved have such divergent interests that it might take a while for things to get sorted out.

items.title: Goodluck India shares surge 17% as merger expands, defence arm to join firm along with green energy unit
items.description: Goodluck India shares surged 17% to a 52-week high of Rs 585 after its board approved the proposed merger of Goodluck Defence and Aerospace and Goodluck Green Energy. The restructuring aims to streamline operations, improve market liquidity and strengthen long-term shareholder value, with further details expected later.

items.title: Dolly Khanna portfolio: Ace investor sells 4 lakh shares of Chennai Petroleum in Q2, stock up 82% in one year
items.description: Ace investor Dolly Khanna trimmed her stake in Chennai Petroleum Corporation by around 3.85 lakh shares in Q2 FY27. The stock has delivered multibagger returns over three and five years, despite recent monthly weakness.

items.title: Will analysts' predictions go wrong? 15 auto stocks with upside potential of up to 50% to as low as negative 1%
items.description: For anyone trying to figure out where the economy is headed in the next six months, the numbers to watch will come from auto showrooms. The auto sector has, for long, provided the earliest indications of the health of the economy. And the sales numbers it puts out ahead of the festive weeks are where the correlation is best seen. So, keep a close watch on the auto pack.

items.title: FIIs cut stakes in 12 stocks in September quarter; shares fall up to 27% in 3 months
items.description: Changes in foreign institutional investor (FII) shareholding often attract market attention, as these investors typically conduct extensive research before making investment decisions. Equally, a reduction in their stake can be worth tracking. Of the BSE 500 companies, around 68 had declared their September 2026 quarter shareholding data so far. Among these, FIIs reduced their stakes in 36 stocks, accounting for more than half of the companies that reported their latest shareholding patterns.Interestingly, several of these stocks underperformed over the past three months. We highlight 12 stocks from this list that declined between 15% and 27% during this period, while FIIs trimmed their holdings in the September 2026 quarter compared with the June 2026 quarter. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: FII ownership hits 17-year low, but foreign holdings in Indian equities rise 3.6 times to $783 billion: Report
items.description: Foreign investor ownership in Indian equities has fallen to a 17-year low of 15.1%, but the absolute value of holdings has risen to around $783 billion. OmniScience Capital attributes the decline in ownership share to faster growth in domestic investor participation.
